title: Euro area HICP flash inflation, June 2026
question: Eurostat euro area all-items HICP annual inflation flash estimate for June 2026, year-on-year percent change, first print
resolutionSource: Eurostat Euro indicators flash estimate release for euro area annual inflation
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first Eurostat flash-estimate print of euro area all-items HICP annual inflation for June 2026, reported to one decimal percent. Use the value first published in the Euro indicators release; ignore later complete HICP releases or revisions.
drivers: May flash inflation already at 3.2 percent
energy contribution still elevated at 10.9 percent year over year
services inflation rose to 3.5 percent in May
recent monthly headline momentum positive but May monthly rate only 0.1 percent
one-decimal Eurostat flash print limits useful precision

reasoning.text: Euro area HICP flash inflation forecast for June 2026
The resolver is the first Eurostat Euro indicators flash-estimate release for euro area all-items HICP annual inflation for June 2026, not the later complete HICP data release or any revision.

reasoning.call: Opened Eurostat HICP overview page for the current inflation news item and data context.
reasoning.result: Eurostat HICP overview listed latest news on 2 June 2026 as euro area annual inflation up to 3.2% and also listed 20 May 2026 annual inflation up to 3.0%.

reasoning.call: Opened Eurostat Euro indicators flash estimate for May 2026.
reasoning.result: Fetched headline all-items HICP annual rates: Jan 2026 1.7, Feb 2026 1.9, Mar 2026 2.6, Apr 2026 3.0, May 2026 3.2e; May monthly rate 0.1e.

reasoning.call: Read the May 2026 Eurostat flash-estimate component table.
reasoning.result: Fetched May 2026 component annual rates: energy 10.9%, services 3.5%, food alcohol and tobacco 2.0%, non-energy industrial goods 0.9%; April comparators were energy 10.8%, services 3.0%, food alcohol and tobacco 2.4%, goods 0.8%.

reasoning.call: Checked Eurostat release scheduling information on the May 2026 flash release and the Euro indicators calendar page.
reasoning.result: The May 2026 flash release says Next release: 1 July 2026; the release-calendar page identifies Inflation as a Euro indicator and states the calendar uses Europe/Luxembourg time zone.

reasoning.text: Base rate/reference class: the last four month-to-month changes in the first-print annual rate were +0.2, +0.7, +0.4, and +0.2 percentage points, but monthly headline inflation in May was only 0.1 percent, so a naive continuation of the rapid March-May rise should be tempered.

Starting from May's 3.2%, I add 0.1 percentage point for continued energy and services pressure but shrink the recent +0.375 average change toward zero because the May monthly rate was only 0.1%; rounded to Eurostat's one-decimal convention this gives 3.3%. An 80% interval of roughly +/-0.55 percentage point around 3.3 rounds to 2.8% to 3.9%.

Counter-consideration: energy inflation was already very high at 10.9% and could mean-revert or face less favorable base effects in June, while food inflation eased to 2.0%; those factors keep the lower side materially plausible despite the high latest headline.
